title: Disconnect a pneumatic line from a push-to-connect manifold port and blank the port
instruction: Disconnect the air line from the manifold and blank off the open port with the plug from the parts tray.
context: Before breaking a pneumatic line, a mechanic isolates and bleeds the stored air: OSHA 1910.147 (control of hazardous energy, lockout/tagout) covers pneumatic energy, and a quarter-turn lockout valve on the supply both shuts the air off and exhausts the downstream side. A line released under pressure whips and can blow debris into eyes. The instruction does not say to close the valve; the robot must do it first, then hold the fitting's collet ring down with one hand while drawing the tube out with the other, and cap the open port with a stem plug so dirt cannot get into the manifold. Done by: industrial machinery mechanics (O*NET 49-9041.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the bench top. Manifold: fixed aluminium block 4 x 12 x 2 cm centred at x 25, y 0, with three push-to-connect ports on top at y 4, 0 and -4. The outer two are already blanked (fixed brass fitting, blue collet ring and grey plug head). Middle port: brass fitting body 1.8 x 1.8 x 1.4 cm with a 0.9 cm bore, and a blue collet ring 1.8 cm square, 0.4 cm tall, that slides down 2 mm against a spring (600 N/m); the collet's teeth grip the tube until the ring is pressed down 1.5 mm. Air line: 8 mm blue polyurethane tube made of rigid segments on spring hinges (about 4 g each), pushed 1.2 cm into the middle fitting, rising 3.8 cm above it, bending over at 7.2 cm and running 16 cm forward (+x) to the port of a fixed pneumatic cylinder (aluminium barrel 10 x 2.6 x 2.6 cm on a mounting foot, brass port at x 41). Supply lockout valve: fixed brass ball-valve body, 2.5 cm cube, at x 25, y 9.5 on the supply pipe (grey, running left along y), joined to the manifold's left end by a brass nipple; its red 6 cm lever starts pointing left along the pipe (open) and turns a quarter turn on a vertical axis toward +x (closed), with 0.08 N*m friction. Parts tray: fixed black block 6 x 6 x 1.2 cm at x 20, y 13 with a 0.9 cm hole holding one spare grey stem plug (4 g; 8 mm square stem 1.6 cm long with a chamfered end, 1.4 cm square head 0.8 cm tall) standing head up.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses (the trial video on a real rig). Valve closed: lever turned 80 deg or more from open. Line off: the tube end's tip 3 mm or more above the collet ring's top (or more than 9 mm off the port's axis) and no gripper within 2 cm of any tube segment. Port blanked: the plug's stem end within 2 mm of the port axis and within 3 mm of the fitting floor, upright within 10 deg, still, and no gripper within 2 cm of it. Score 0 if the collet ring was ever pressed down 1.5 mm (releasing the tube) while the valve was not closed, latched for the episode, and 0 if the valve is not closed at the end. Otherwise 1.0 line off and port blanked, success when held 1 s; 0.5 line off, port not blanked; 0.1 valve closed only. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Turn the valve lever back to open (along the pipe), push the tube back into the middle fitting with the run laid into the cylinder's port, and stand the plug head up in the tray's hole.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction. No air is simulated: a disconnect with the valve open does not whip the line; it only latches a score of 0. The collet is a spring-loaded slider, and its grip on the tube is a joint that is removed for the rest of the episode once the ring is pressed down 1.5 mm; the plug is held in the bore only by fit and gravity (no collet teeth on it). The tube is a chain of rigid square segments on spring hinges, its far end resting in the cylinder's port rather than gripped. The bore has 0.5 mm of play on each side of the tube. Fittings, plug and tube have square sections.
